newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador finance minister says offered resignation.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador finance minister says offered resignation.

text.p: Ecuador's Finance Minister Carlos Davalos said Thursday he has offered his resignation to President Fabian Alarcon.
Davalos told journalists he presented his resignation "some days ago. I will stay on until he (Alarcon) decides."
The minister added that he did not know whether Danilo Carrera, the president of the monetary board and Fidel Jaramillo, the general manager of the central bank, had done the same.

"I am talking about myself. I have no idea of the others," he said. Davalos made the statements minutes before departing to Washington with Jaramillo, to meet with International Monetary Fund officials.

Since a referendum at the end of May approved of Alarcon's mandate after the ousting of former President Abdala Bucaram earlier in the year, several members of the government have offered their resignations as a good will gesture to give Alarcon a free hand in chosing ministers.
"As I have always said, I am a friend of the president and I do not want to cause him any problems, least of all political problems as he has expressed confidence in me as a minister," Davalos said.
Local newspapers Thursday speculated government economic officials had offered their resignations because of disagreements with Alarcon on economic policy.
Earlier Thursday, administration secretary Arturo Gangotena said he knew nothing of the resignation of the economic officials.
"As far as I know there are no resignations, they are travelling to Washington. As such I would say that in general terms they are continuing to work with the same enthusiasm," Gangotena said.
